The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 and requested this Court to set aside the Arbitral Award dated 08.12.2021 passed in case No.LAQ/ARB/NH- 07/CR/4/2020-21 by the respondent No. 2.
2.
In the petition it is stated that National Highways Authority of India was constituted by an Act of the Parliament, "the National Highways Authority of A.P. No.57/2022 India Act, 1988" .

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is responsible for the development, maintenance and management of National Highways entrusted to it and for matters connected thereto.

3. It is stated that the Central Government for the purpose of widening/up-gradation, maintenance,
management and operation of NH-7 on the stretch of land from 524.720 to kms. 556.840 of Hyderabad - Bengaluru Section issued preliminary notification dated 09.12.2009 under Section 3-A(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956 in-respect of acquisition of lands situated at Venkatala village, Yelahanka Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluka.

The final notification was published in the official Gazette on 02.07.2010.
4.

It is stated that under the said notification for 1st stage of acquisition, amongst other lands the NA lands in survey No.18/2 to an extent of 4304 sq.ft and in Sy.No.18/3 to an extent of 1076 sq.ft.
situated at the above said village were also acquired.
. It is stated that respondent No.3 was appointed as the competent authority.

The respondent No.3 vide award dated 24.05.2011 determined the market value of non-agricultural lands at Rs.1,314/-
per sq. feet.
In order to determine the market value, the respondent No.3 obtained the sale statistics for the period from 08-12-2008 to 09-12-2009 as well as guidance value for the relevant period.
The respondent No. 3 observed that the average of the sale statistics was Rs. 1,075/-per sq.ft.
The guidance value which came into effect from 19.04.2007,provided the guidance value of NA lands as Rs. 1,000/- per sq. feet.

Since both the average of the sale statistics as well as the guidance value were on the lower side, the respondent No.3 relied upon the market value already determined for NA lands situated in the adjacent village Hunasamaranahalli which was Rs. 1314/- per sq. feet.

Accordingly, the respondent No. 3 determined the market value of NA lands at Rs. 1,314/- per sq.

Section 24(3) of the Act provides provision regarding hearing and written proceedings.

It reads thus:
"All statements, documents or other information supplied to, or applications made to the aribral tribunal by one party shall be communicated to the other party, and any expert report or evidentiary document on which the arbital tribunal may rely in making its decision shall be communicated to the parties".
